```{exercise}
The following is an adaptation of exercise 6.53 from [Ross: A first course in probability](https://www.pearson.com/en-us/pearsonplus/p/9780138027889).
Let $(X, Y)$ be a bivariate random variable with $X \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 1)$ and $Y \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 1)$.
Let $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$ and $\Theta = \tan^{-1}(Y / X)$.

Find the joint PDF of $(R, \Theta)$.
```

<div class="fold">
```{solution, echo = togs}
Define: $f([x, y]) = [r, \theta]$.
The inverse is $f^{-1}([r, \theta]) = [r \cos \theta, r \sin \theta]$. We want to find $p_{R\Theta}(r, \theta)$ by applying the change-of-variables formula:
\begin{align}
  p_{R\Theta}([r, \theta]) = p_{XY}(f^{-1}([r, \theta])) |\det J_{f^{-1}} ([r, \theta])|.
\end{align}
Since $X, Y \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 1)$, we conclude that $p_XY([x, y]) = 1$ for all valid inputs $x, y \in [0, 1]$.

The Jacobian of $f^{-1}$ equals:
\begin{align}
  J_{f^{-1}} = \begin{bmatrix}
  \frac{\partial r \cos \theta}{\partial r} & \frac{\partial r \cos \theta}{\partial \theta} \\
  \frac{\partial r \sin \theta}{\partial r} & \frac{\partial r \sin \theta}{\partial \theta}
\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}
  \cos \theta & -r \sin \theta \\
  \sin \theta & r \cos \theta
\end{bmatrix}.
\end{align}

The determinant equals:
\begin{align}
\det J_{f^{-1}} &= \cos \theta \cdot r \cos \theta - (\sin \theta \cdot (-\sin \theta)) \\
                &= r (\cos \theta)^2 + r (\sin \theta)^2 = r ((\cos \theta)^2 + (\sin \theta)^2) = r.
\end{align}

The final joint density is thus:
\begin{align}
  p_{R\Theta}([r, \theta]) &= p_{XY}(f^{-1}([r, \theta])) |\det J_{f^{-1}} ([r, \theta])| \\
                           &= 1 |r| = r.
\end{align}
```
</div>
